problem: The Eulerian field is built from one particle's path only. One path gives u and v along that path, not u and v at every point in space. Saying 'u = 2 m/s everywhere' and 'v = 3(x − 1) m/s' is an extra assumption, and a student may wrongly conclude that a single Lagrangian trajectory always yields the full field.
fix: State the assumption before eliminating t: assume the flow is steady and the horizontal component is u = 2 m/s everywhere. Then v = 3(x − 1) m/s follows. Add one line: a full field needs a family of paths R(r0, t), not a single path.

problem: 'the two-part acceleration is in velocity and acceleration of fluid particles' is a dangling cross-reference to another chapter. A student reading only this unit does not learn that the two parts are the local term ∂V/∂t and the convective term (V·∇)V.
fix: Name the two parts: 'the total acceleration has a local part ∂V/∂t (zero in steady flow) and a convective part (V·∇)V (not zero when speed changes along the path). The derivation is in the chapter on velocity and acceleration of fluid particles.'

problem: 'The mass inside a control volume is not fixed' is true in general but reads as if the mass inside a fixed control volume always changes. In steady flow through a fixed control volume the mass inside is constant, even though mass keeps crossing the surface.
fix: Say: 'The mass inside a control volume can change with time when the flow is unsteady. In steady flow with a fixed control volume it stays constant, but mass still crosses the control surface. Only a system has fixed mass by definition.'
